nm_05_the_transition_zone.blurb: A wall on the Palomas Peak cliff band above Placitas, reached by walking the base trail beyond the Showdown Wall and a few breaks in the rock. Twelve climbs, ten of them sport and two trad, on limestone. The grades start around 5.8 and climb to the low 5.11s, with most of the lines at 5.10 and 5.11, so it suits a solid 5.10 leader more than a beginner. The terrain is varied: stucco-coloured slabs, a buttress with several small roofs, pocket pulling and a few cracks. Some routes begin right above the trail. Anchors are fixed lowering hardware, so bring a standard sport rack plus a few cams for the trad lines.

nm_03_the_franks.blurb: A short, steep section of the Palomas Peak limestone above Placitas, sitting between the Slab and the Showdown Wall. All twelve routes are sport, and the difficulty is serious: one route in the 5.11s, then mostly 5.12 and 5.13 with a couple of 5.14s. The wall bulges hard, overhanging severely for the first few feet before easing to vertical, so most lines are a brutal boulder problem followed by easier climbing. Several lines are unfinished projects. Expect to share it with very few people, and bring a full set of quickdraws and strong fingers rather than a trad rack.

nm_balcony_the.blurb: A terrace of three small formations a short way up and right of Super Slab in the El Rito sport climbing zone of northern New Mexico. The twelve routes are all bolted and sit on the area's cobble-studded conglomerate, where pockets, bulges and coloured streaks make the holds. Grades run from 5.9 into the 5.11s, with most lines at 5.9 and 5.10, so it is a friendly place for climbers stepping up. Belay with care near the base, since loose rock can fall onto the busier slab below.

nm_capitan_gap.blurb: A small, quiet crag centred on a granite spire at roughly 7,200 feet, about an hour from Ruidoso. The twelve lines are a mixed bag: five sport routes, a few boulder problems, two top-ropes and two trad lines. Boulder problems stay easy (VB to V2), the roped climbs range from 5.7 to 5.10 with a couple of harder ones, and one 5.13 offwidth project is waiting. The rock is patinated granite with decent rests. It sees few visitors, and the road in is rough enough that a high-clearance vehicle is wise. A short uphill walk from the pullout reaches the base.

nm_eden_wall_north_sector.blurb: The first sector you meet on the Eden Wall trail in the Diablo Canyon area north of Santa Fe, about 6,000 feet up. Twelve climbs, almost all sport with a single trad line, on quality rock that is steeper than it looks from below. Grades start at 5.10 and run to a 5.13, with the bulk of the routes between 5.11 and 5.12, making it a good stop for intermediate to strong sport climbers. Large junipers at the base offer shade, which helps on early-morning arrivals, since the wall faces east and catches the sun first.
